question: How have CH4 and N2O changed, and are they growing faster or slower than CO2 in relative terms?
summary: From 2001 to 2025, atmospheric concentrations of all three greenhouse gases increased, and CO2 showed the highest relative growth. CO2 rose 14.86% overall, compared with 9.30% for CH4 and 7.11% for N2O. On an annualized basis, CO2 grew at 0.579% per year, CH4 at 0.371% and N2O at 0.287%. In percentage terms, CH4 accumulated slower than CO2 and N2O accumulated slower than CO2.
